The rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis is phosphofructokinase (PFK), which catalyzes the phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.  
This step is a key regulatory point because PFK is allosterically inhibited by ATP and citrate, and activated by AMP and ADP, allowing the cell to control glycolytic flux according to energy needs.
